"""Headline title casing for article and newsletter titles."""

SMALL_WORDS = frozenset({
    "a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "but", "by", "for", "in", "nor",
    "of", "on", "or", "per", "the", "to", "via",
})

_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = ".,:;!?"


def title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` in headline title case.

    ``text`` is split on single spaces into words. Each word is converted on
    its own and the words are joined again with single spaces:

    1. A word with an uppercase letter anywhere after its first character
       (such as "iPhone", "NASA" or "McKinsey") is kept exactly as written.
    2. Otherwise, if the word with any trailing ``.,:;!?`` characters removed
       is, in lowercase, one of ``SMALL_WORDS`` (a, an, and, as, at, but, by,
       for, in, nor, of, on, or, per, the, to, via), the word is written in
       lowercase -- unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``, in
       which case its first character is uppercased.
    3. Every other word has its first character uppercased.
    """
    words = text.split(" ")
    result = []
    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        if index > 0 and word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() in SMALL_WORDS:
            result.append(word.lower())
        else:
            result.append(word.capitalize())
    return " ".join(result)

"""Headline title casing for article and newsletter titles."""

SMALL_WORDS = frozenset({
    "a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "but", "by", "for", "in", "nor",
    "of", "on", "or", "per", "the", "to", "via",
})

_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = ".,:;!?"


def title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` in headline title case.

    ``text`` is split on single spaces into words. Each word is converted on
    its own and the words are joined again with single spaces:

    1. A word with an uppercase letter anywhere after its first character
       (such as "iPhone", "NASA" or "McKinsey") is kept exactly as written.
    2. Otherwise, if the word with any trailing ``.,:;!?`` characters removed
       is, in lowercase, one of ``SMALL_WORDS`` (a, an, and, as, at, but, by,
       for, in, nor, of, on, or, per, the, to, via), the word is written in
       lowercase -- unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``, in
       which case its first character is uppercased.
    3. Every other word has its first character uppercased.

    Additionally, the first word after a colon is treated as the start of a
    subtitle and has its first character uppercased.
    """
    words = text.split(" ")
    result = []
    last_index = len(words) - 1
    capitalize_next = False

    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        # Rule 1: Preserve mixed-case words (uppercase after first char)
        if any(c.isupper() for c in word[1:]):
            result.append(word)
        # Rule 2: Small words stay lowercase (unless first, last, or after colon)
        elif (index > 0 and
              index < last_index and
              not capitalize_next and
              word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() in SMALL_WORDS):
            result.append(word.lower())
        # Rule 3: Capitalize first letter of other words
        else:
            result.append(word.capitalize())

        # Track if next word starts a subtitle (after colon)
        capitalize_next = word.endswith(':')

    return " ".join(result)
